role.q: An application is down for all users. What are your first 15 minutes?
role.model: Confirm the impact and log a P1 ticket. Check monitoring and recent changes (deployments, configuration, certificates), and verify the basics: processes running, disk, memory, database, network. Communicate early to stakeholders with the impact and next update time. Restore service as fast as possible, for example by rollback or restart, escalating early if needed, and investigate the root cause afterwards.

role.q: How do you prioritise your ticket queue?
role.model: With an impact × urgency matrix aligned with the SLAs: critical services and many users first, then by SLA deadline. I re-evaluate when new information arrives, group related tickets that may share a cause, and keep requesters informed when their ticket waits.

role.q: A user reports that 'the application is slow'. How do you investigate?
role.model: Clarify first: which screen or action, since when, for one user or many, which location or browser. Reproduce if possible. Then check monitoring: response time, error rate, server resources, database slow queries, and recent changes. Narrow down to the network, the application or the database, and keep the user informed.

role.q: What is the difference between an incident and a problem?
role.model: An incident is an unplanned interruption or degradation that we restore as fast as possible. A problem is the underlying cause of one or more incidents, which we investigate to remove so it does not happen again; until then, a known error with a workaround is documented.

role.q: Tell me about a recurring issue you eliminated.
role.model: Our batch failed about twice a month because of a full disk. I opened a problem, found that logs were never rotated, configured log rotation and an alert at 80% disk usage, and documented a runbook. The incident did not happen again, saving roughly four hours of night interventions a month.

role.q: How do you communicate with users during a major incident?
role.why: Communication is half of incident management.
role.model: Early and on a fixed rhythm, for example every 30 minutes for a P1, even without news. Each message says the impact, what we know, what we are doing, a workaround if any, and the next update time. Plain language, no blame, and a final message when it is resolved with a short explanation.

role.q: Which commands or tools do you use to investigate on a Linux server?
role.model: systemctl status and journalctl for services, tail and grep on logs, top or htop for CPU and memory, df -h and du for disk, ss for listening ports, curl to test endpoints, and SQL queries on the database to check data. Then the observability tools of the team, such as Grafana, Kibana or Splunk.

role.q: How do you make sure knowledge is shared in the support team?
role.why: Teams need resilience beyond one expert.
role.model: Document fixes in the knowledge base as I go, write runbooks for recurring incidents, link them from alerts and tickets, run short post-mortems, and pair on complex tickets so more than one person knows each system.
